mechanism: A cold-email pattern: several subject and opening variants of one offer, sent as a three-step plain-text sequence with short gaps between steps. Plain text avoids tracking pixels and heavy HTML, which helps deliverability; variants let the sender compare reply rates per step. The numbers come from the sender's own sending tool and reply counts.
claim: A three-step plain-text sequence with spin-tax variants gets replies from local businesses for AI website sales.
why_not_testable: Measuring replies needs real sends to real prospects, which is a sending account and a list, not a keyless run.
needs: a sending domain, a prospect list and weeks of reply data
one_line: A three-step plain-text cold email sequence with spun variants is the unit to A/B; only real reply counts can judge it.
idea_why: Short plain-text sequences are standard and sound, but the reply lift from variants is only knowable from a live send.
breakdown: Write one offer and three to five variants of subject and opener, then three steps: first touch, a short bump, a last line. Load them into a sender with per-variant tagging, split the list evenly, and log replies per variant and step. Under UK rules it needs a lawful basis and an opt-out line for corporate subscribers. A person would build and clean the prospect list and read the replies, which no script covers.
